text:
maya: quick flag — noticed ~12 leads routed to overflow this AM even though EMEA SDR queue was green. looks correlated with enrichment timeouts. anyone seen this pattern?

alex: yup caught it in the routing logs. enrichment webhook latency spike around 08:20 PST, many requests >45s so our enrichment timeout (30s) expired and we fell back to round-robin overflow.

sophia: ugh. that's the case where HS returns but after claim window expired, right? salesforce mapping then drops owner and rr takes over.

alex: exact sequence: HS webhook delayed, enrichment lambda retries but after the claim TTL (35s) we mark as unowned. fallback policy triggers. here's the config we currently have: 

```json
{"enrichment_timeout_ms":30000, "claim_ttl_ms":35000, "fallback_policy":"round_robin_overflow"}
```

lauren: if enrichment is flaky during peak imports we should either bump timeouts or make claim TTL longer. bumping both increases risk of longer lock times but avoids churn. suggestion: bump enrichment_timeout_ms -> 60000 and claim_ttl_ms -> 70000 for a canary window.

maya: canary sounds good. small % of traffic? 5% to start and monitor claim success rate + lead-age.

alex: agree. also adding a quick patch: when enrichment webhook returns owner assignment after fallback, we should attempt owner re-assign instead of letting rr keep it. small idempotent flow: if contact.external_id and enrichment.owner present -> try reassign.

sophia: tricky with SF mapping because some integrations treat reassign as an update and trigger workflows. we should gate reassigns to only when enrichment.source == "hs_enrichment_v2" and enrichment.score > 0.7.

lauren: ops checklist for rollout:
- deploy canary config (5%)
- enable extra logging for claim lifecycle (claim_acquire, claim_expire, fallback_trigger)
- observe for 12h and measure % leads to overflow (goal <0.1%)
- if stable, ramp to 50% then 100%

maya: @alex can you draft the config PR and include rollback steps? i'll own the smoke metrics dashboard.

alex: on it. PR will include: code + migration for claim TTL and a new opt-in flag `reassign_after_enrichment`. default false. sample patch: 

```diff
- "enrichment_timeout_ms": 30000,
- "claim_ttl_ms": 35000,
+ "enrichment_timeout_ms": 60000,
+ "claim_ttl_ms": 70000,
+ "reassign_after_enrichment": true
```

hubspot-bot: HubSpot sync: contact 00345abc updated (enrichment complete) — processing time 49s.

alex: ^ that one is an example we saw. with reassign_after_enrichment enabled that contact would be picked back up. need to ensure we don't reassign if owner already took action in SF. add a last_activity check.

sophia: last_activity < enrichment.timestamp is a good guard. also, add a rate-limit on reassigns per-user to avoid notification storms.

lauren: can we add a brief runbook entry for support? if a rep reports missing lead, check:
1) routing logs for claim_acquire/expire
2) hs webhook latency
3) enrichment status
4) last_activity in SF
5) manual reassign steps (if auto-reassign disabled)

maya: thanks. i'll add runbook notes and update the dashboard alerts (enrichment_latency_p95 > 40s, overflow_rate > 0.1%).

alex: deploying canary PR to staging now. will post PR link here when ready.

maya: great — circle back after 12h smoke. :thumbsup:

lauren: tagging the support rota so they're aware of possible noise during ramp: @support-team

sophia: one more thing — let's log the enrichment source/version so we can quickly filter v1 vs v2 failures. small schema change but helpful.

alex: noted. adding `enrichment_source` field to the log envelope.

maya: thanks team. follow-ups: PR link, dashboard, and runbook update.

alex: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/lead-routing/pull/842 (draft)

maya: got it. monitoring started.
